## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts

- Monocular 3D pose estimation in cluttered environments
- Scene graphs and graph neural networks for relational reasoning
- Grasp affordances for robotic manipulation
- On-device meta-learning (3-shot adaptation)
- Synthetic-to-real domain transfer strategies

## Code Example

```python
# Pseudo-code: update_scene_graph for a frame
def update_scene_graph(frame, model, device='cuda'):
    features = model.backbone(frame)
    detections = model.detector(features)
    poses = model.pose_head(features, detections)
    scene_graph = model.gnn_head(detections, poses)
    affordances = model.affordance_head(features, detections)
    return {
        'objects': detections,
        'poses': poses,
        'relations': scene_graph,
        'affordances': affordances
    }
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design an end-to-end, edge-ready computer vision system that handles unseen objects through few-shot adaptation while satisfying strict latency and accuracy constraints. It probes understanding of the full ML pipeline: from data strategy and architecture design to loss functions and evaluation rigor.

## Key Concepts

- Real-time monocular 6-DoF pose estimation from single RGB stream
- Differentiable rendering for pose refinement and novel view synthesis
- Synthetic data generation with domain randomization plus real data capture
- Temporal consistency across frames using recurrent modules or pose smoothing
- Occlusion handling via attention mechanisms and uncertainty estimation
- On-device 5-shot adaptation using lightweight adapter modules

## Data Strategy

**Synthetic Data:** Generate photorealistic renders of 500+ utensil CAD models with domain randomization (lighting, textures, backgrounds, camera poses). Use physics-based simulation to generate grasp annotations.

**Real Data:** Capture 10K+ real images with multi-view annotations via RGB-D scanning and manual labeling. Apply domain randomization during training (color jitter, blur, weather effects).

## Losses

- **Pose Loss:** L1/L2 on rotation (quaternion) and translation, plus edge-edge distance (Chamfer distance)
- **Grip State Loss:** Binary cross-entropy for open/closed classification
- **Occlusion Loss:** Mask IoU loss for learned visibility prediction; penalize invisible keypoints
- **Temporal Consistency Loss:** Smooth L1 on pose deltas between consecutive frames; enforce kinematic feasibility
- **Rendering Loss:** Photo-metric loss between rendered and observed RGB for self-supervision

## Adaptation Workflow

1. Pre-train on synthetic + real data for seen categories
2. At deployment, capture 5 views of the new unseen utensil (robot holds it in known poses)
3. Freeze backbone; fine-tune lightweight adapters for 50–100 iterations on edge device
4. Run inference with adapted model; update adapters online if performance degrades

## Evaluation Metrics

- **ADD(-S) / AUC:** Mean 3D error for pose accuracy under symmetry
- **Grip Accuracy:** F1-score for open/closed state classification
- **Inference Latency:** Measured on target edge GPU (Jetson Orin / NVIDIA T4)
- **Adaptation Quality:** Pose error after 5-shot fine-tuning
- **Occlusion Robustness:** mAP under varying visible-fraction thresholds

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pipeline sketch
function pipeline(frame, adapters, known_objects) {
  const detections = detector.infer(frame);
  const crops = crop_and_resize(frame, detections);
  
  const poses = crops.map(crop => {
    const features = backbone.extract(crop);
    const adapted = adapters.apply(features, known_objects);
    const {pose, grip, mask} = decoder.predict(adapted);
    return {pose, grip, mask, confidence: detections.conf};
  });
  
  return temporal_smoother.smooth(poses);
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design real-time computer vision systems for deformable objects—a challenging, underexplored problem requiring novel representations, robust on-device adaptation, and efficient inference on constrained hardware.

## Key Concepts
- Deformable object pose and mesh parameterization
- Differentiable rendering for multi-view supervision
- Temporal tracking and occlusion handling
- On-device meta-learning for few-shot adaptation

## Architecture
- **Backbone**: A CNN+Transformer hybrid encoder extracts spatial features and models global context
- **Per-Item Head**: Dedicated regression branches predict bounding boxes, keypoint heatmaps, and mesh deformation parameters
- **Deformable Mesh Module**: A graph neural network operates on a predefined garment template, predicting vertex offsets conditioned on image features
- **Differentiable Renderer**: Projects 3D meshes to 2D silhouettes and depth maps for photometric and geometric consistency loss

## Data Strategy
- Synthetic training data generated via physics-based simulation (e.g., BlenderCloth, MuJoCo) with randomized fabric properties, lighting, and camera angles
- Real-world data collection with multi-view RGB-D cameras and manual mesh annotations
- Domain randomization to bridge sim-to-real gap, varying texture, wrinkle patterns, and motion blur

## Losses
- **Geometric**: L1 loss on projected keypoints and silhouette IoU between rendered and observed masks
- **Pose**: Smooth L1 loss on 3D joint coordinates with temporal consistency regularization
- **Mesh**: Chamfer distance on visible vertices and normal consistency for fold boundaries
- **Adversarial**: Optional GAN loss for realism when adapting to novel textiles

## 3-Shot On-Device Adaptation Workflow
1. **Meta-learning pretraining**: Train model on diverse garment categories using Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) to learn a good weight initialization
2. **Edge deployment**: Ship frozen backbone with lightweight adapter layers (e.g., LoRA-style residual modules)
3. **On-device adaptation**: Given 3 labeled frames of a new garment, update only adapter weights via gradient descent with a frozen teacher branch providing consistency regularization
4. **Inference**: Run adapted model at <40 ms/frame using INT8 quantization and operator fusion on the edge accelerator (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson, Qualcomm DSP)

## Evaluation Metrics
- **Detection**: mAP@0.5 for bounding box localization
- **Segmentation**: IoU and boundary F-score for garment masks
- **Pose**: MPJPE (mean per-joint position error) in 3D and ADD-S for symmetric garments
- **Mesh**: Per-vertex error and normal consistency score
- **Adaptation**: Performance delta between pretrained and 3-shot adapted models
- **Latency**: Frame throughput and P99 latency on target hardware
